title: Best Heated Clothes Airers UK
short: Heated airers and drying pods compared by capacity, wattage, timers and running cost.
intro: A heated clothes airer dries laundry indoors for a fraction of the cost of a tumble dryer, and without leaving a room full of damp air the way a plain rack does. This guide compares the models Mumsnet's panel picked, from slimline airers for small flats to drying pods for big loads.

products.name: 3-Tier Heated Airer
products.summary: Mumsnet's top pick has three tiers and 21 metres of heated rail, enough for a full load. It is light and folds away, though it has no timer and is often out of stock.
pros: Large drying space for full loads

products.name: Deluxe 3-Tier Heated Airer
products.best_for: Big households that want a built-in timer
products.summary: A step-up version with a timer of up to 12 hours and eye-level controls. Mumsnet says it can hold two large loads, and it folds compactly.

products.name: Wing 12m Heated Airer with Cover
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a full-load airer at a lower price
products.summary: A sturdy yet lightweight winged airer that holds a full load and comes with a cover. It takes up a lot of room when open and can topple with heavy items.
products.search: Minky Wing 12m heated airer with cover

products.name: Drying Pod
products.best_for: Delicates and small loads that need drying fast
products.summary: A heated pod that fits over a rack and dries items in about 2-3 hours while reducing creases. It costs far more per hour to run and is loud.
cons: Fiddly to assemble and take apart
Needs to be hung over rails

products.name: Sure Dri Heat Pod Drying System
products.best_for: People who already own a standard 3-tier airer
products.summary: A heated pod that turns an ordinary 3-tier airer into a drying pod, drying a full load in about three hours, at the cost of a fiddly setup.
pros: Turns a standard airer into a heated pod
Dries full loads in about 3 hours

products.name: Slimline Heated Airer
products.summary: A small, low-power airer with a minimal footprint that stores flat. It is very cheap to run but cannot cope with a full load.
cons: Larger items use all the space

guide.q: Is a heated airer cheaper than a tumble dryer?
guide.a: Usually yes. Heated airers use a few hundred watts, while tumble dryers draw much more. Mumsnet's estimates for the airers here run from about 3p to 10p an hour. Your actual cost depends on how long you run it and your tariff.
Drying clothes indoors releases moisture into the air whatever you use. Ventilate the room, or use a dehumidifier in the same room, to avoid condensation building up.

guide.q: What size of heated airer do I need?
guide.a: Look at the rail length and stated capacity. Around 15-16kg or 12-21m of rail handles a full family load. For a couple or one person, a slimline model is often enough.

guide.q: Is it safe to leave a heated airer on?
guide.a: Follow the manufacturer's instructions, keep the cable clear, do not overload it, and do not cover it in ways the instructions do not allow. A timer is a useful safety feature if you like to leave it running.
